claim: For each fixed finite sparse bipartite support E, fixed finite k_ji>=1, and fixed positive finite rate vector, the paired network 0<->A_j, A_j<->A_j+B_i, A_j+B_i<->(k_ji+1)A_j+B_i is irreducible, nonexplosive in physical time, and positive recurrent on each class obtained by fixing isolated-substrate counts.
quantifiers: Fix finite J,I,E and all k_ji. For every fixed rate vector with all six rates positive and finite on each catalyst and included edge, every fixed isolated-substrate label class has one closed irreducible active-coordinate chain with a unique invariant probability.
limits: Family-specific. Isolated substrates are frozen labels. Does not cover missing reverse channels, zero rates, arbitrary propensities, or general weakly reversible networks. The proof is internal and has no external validation or priority status.

source.citation: Anderson and Kim, Some Network Conditions for Positive Recurrence of Stochastically Modeled Reaction Networks, 2018, Theorem 3.1 (CTMC Foster criterion).
source.use: Abstract CTMC Foster criterion only; network-specific drift and physical-time nonexplosion are separately proved.

claim: For each fixed finite sparse paired-edge structure and compact rectangular rate box with strictly positive lower and finite upper endpoints, there exist one class-relative support-corrected exponential V and common C,c>0 such that L_theta V<=C-cV for every active state and every rate vector in the box.
quantifiers: The constants and V are independent of theta and of isolated-substrate labels after projection to active coordinates. V is norm-like on every fixed label class; if no isolated substrates exist it is norm-like on the full lattice.
proof_object: outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_geometric_drift/ROOT_AUDIT.txt; explicit rational alternative in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_certificate_effectivity/REPORT.txt; independent adversarial audit in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_switch_adversarial/AUDIT.txt.
mechanism: High inactive B_i counts receive negative local-neighbor immigration switch drift. High active B_i counts receive q-removal drift; each sole-neighbor death surcharge is paired with the same active edge. Catalysts with no high adjacent substrate are controlled by the strict R-near-one death margin when all adjacent B counts are zero, or by a reverse falling-factorial term when some bounded adjacent count is positive.
limits: Uniformity is not claimed as rate lower endpoints approach zero or R approaches one. It is not a complete recurrence recognition theorem and does not cover arbitrary weakly reversible networks. Independent external proof review and novelty remain open.
evidence: Exact formula check on 4096 states in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_counterexample/verify_independent.py.
Exact rational certificate fixture on 625 states in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_certificate_effectivity/synthesize_fixture.py.
Exact rate-box drift fixture on 10404 states in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_physical_clock/check_rate_box.py.

claim: For the paired sparse family with fixed finite E and k_ji and a supplied strictly positive rational rectangular rate box, an explicit terminating construction outputs rational support-switch potential parameters, thresholds, and c,C satisfying the common generator drift inequality.
cost: The report claims polynomial binary-input bit size and construction time under standard exact integer/rational arithmetic; thresholds may be numerically large, and no polynomial mixing-time bound is claimed.
limits: This is a sufficient certificate compiler for a promised network grammar and positive rational box, not a necessary-and-sufficient recurrence recognizer. Failure or inapplicability outside the interface leaves recurrence UNKNOWN. External review remains open.

claim: Under the sparse common geometric drift on a compact positive rate box, every active quotient skeleton has a common finite drift set and common one-step minorization to the active origin. Standard drift/minorization therefore gives V-geometric convergence with common constants over rate vectors and isolated-substrate labels.
quantifiers: There are M'<infinity and gamma>0, common to theta and label z, with ||P_t^(theta,z)(x,.)-pi_(theta,z)||_V<=M' V(x) exp(-gamma t) for every t>=0 and x in the class. The prefactor scales with V(x); uniform convergence over all initial states in ordinary total variation is not claimed.
proof_object: outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_geometric_drift/ROOT_AUDIT.txt; complete-pair quantitative version in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/uniform_mixing/PROOF.txt; exact primary theorem gate in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/geometric_ergodicity_prior/REPORT.txt.

source.citation: Meyn and Tweedie, Stability of Markovian Processes III: Foster-Lyapunov Criteria for Continuous-Time Processes, Advances in Applied Probability 25(3), 518-548 (1993), Theorem 6.1 and CD3; discrete-time input Theorem 6.3 of Part I (1992).
source.use: Fixed-process V-geometric theorem. Uniformity over the parameter box is derived from the additional common drift, explicit finite-path minorization, and common bounds; the published theorem alone is not parameterized.

limits: Full-state minorizing measures depend on frozen isolated-substrate labels; the theorem is applied on the quotient and lifted class by class. Constants can be extremely poor.

claim: Uniform tightness or a common coercive stationary-moment bound over all full-state class invariant laws is false when the network has an isolated substrate whose conserved label ranges over all nonnegative integers.
counterexample: Take E empty, one catalyst with 0<->A, and one inert B. Class z has stationary law Pois(alpha/delta) tensor delta_z. For any finite set F, choose z above all B counts in F; then pi_z(F)=0. Also E_pi_z exp(eta B)=exp(eta z).
proof_object: outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_stationarity_clock/REPORT.txt, section ISOLATED-CLASS OBSTRUCTION TO FULL-STATE UNIFORMITY; the same quantifier distinction is in sparse_classwise_audit/REPORT.txt.
limits: This is cross-class label escape. Each fixed class is well behaved, and active-coordinate marginals are identical across labels. It is not a within-class recurrence or tightness failure.

claim: Anderson-Cappelletti-Fan-Kim (2025), Corollary 3.5, covers the complex-balanced subfamily of the sparse paired-edge target, including arbitrary finite k_ji, under its layered catalyzed-birth/death hypotheses. The target has the required open catalyst species and each active substrate has a neighbor supplying a reversible catalyzed birth/death pair.

source.citation: Anderson, Cappelletti, Fan, and Kim, A New Path Method for Exponential Ergodicity of Markov Processes on Z^d, with Applications to Stochastic Reaction Networks, SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems 24(2) (2025), 1668-1710, Corollary 3.5, DOI 10.1137/24M1665933.
source.use: L2 exponential ergodicity for fixed complex-balanced parameter vectors satisfying the stated structural condition.

limits: Complex balance imposes exact rate equalities. This does not establish arbitrary-rate recurrence or a parameter-uniform rate-box spectral gap.

claim: Separate fixed-positive-rate extensions add (i) arbitrary reversible first-order catalyst conversions, (ii) arbitrary reversible substrate transfers, or (iii) arbitrary catalytic cross-feed pairs to the complete-pair family and prove physical-time nonexplosive positive recurrence in each stated branch.
limits: The branches are separate. The proof does not cover their arbitrary union, sparse catalyst-substrate support, uniform parameter boxes, or general weakly reversible networks. The failure of one total-substrate potential for cross-feeds is not a recurrence counterexample.

claim: For one stated three-species open network with A+B<->A+C and a specified compact positive rate box, the full lattice is one irreducible positive-recurrent class, sup_theta E_pi[A+B+C]<=49, and both substrate isomers have strictly positive uniform stationary occupation floors.
limits: The model is a coarse open reaction motif, not an atom-balanced finite-resource mechanism. The occupation floors are exact but extremely small. No global deterministic attraction or novelty claim is made.

claim: No general higher-dimensional weakly reversible recurrence theorem or qualifying within-class transient, null-recurrent, or explosive counterexample was obtained.
reason: Published general criteria audited here leave a reachable catalyst-free high-substrate tier outside their sufficient hypotheses. The reported two-species all-rate claim remains source-reported in checked materials. Failure of a certificate is not evidence of nonrecurrence.

source.citation: Anderson, Cappelletti, Kim (2020), Theorems 4.1 and 6.1; Anderson and Kim (2018), tier criteria; source report outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_theorem_coverage/REPORT.txt.
source.use: Primary-source scope audit only; sufficient criteria do not cover the target's arbitrary-rate higher-order boundary.

claim: The deterministic N33 permanence and N54 PDE barrier results are separate from the stochastic CTMC theorem in this cycle and are not used as recurrence premises.
limits: No ODE-to-jump recurrence transfer is claimed. Falling-factorial propensities, CTMC irreducibility, nonexplosion, and physical holding times are handled directly in the stochastic proofs.

claim: The unchanged support-switch potential V=a1+a2+R^b1(1+h)+R^b2(1+h)+K*1_{a1+a2=0}, h=1_{a1+a2=0}, does not yield a Foster negative drift for every weakly reversible extension of the complete paired family.
quantifiers: At all rates 1 and k=1, add A1+B1<->A2+B2 and B1+B2->A1+B1+B2->A1+A2+B1+B2->B1+B2. For R=6/5,K=2 and x_n=(1,1,n,n), the exact generator value is (6/5)^n(2n^2-3n/5+4/5)+2n^2+4n, which is positive and diverges.
counterexample: This four-species network is complex balanced at c*=(1,1,1,1), irreducible on N_0^4, and has stationary product Pois(1)^4; the counterexample is to this instantiated unchanged Lyapunov ansatz, not to recurrence, nonexplosion, or other Lyapunov functions.

source.citation: Anderson, Cappelletti, Koyama, and Kurtz, Non-explosivity of stochastically modeled reaction networks that are complex balanced (2018).
source.use: Primary theorem for nonexplosion of the complex-balanced example.

source.citation: Anderson, Craciun, and Kurtz, Product-form stationary distributions for deficiency zero chemical reaction networks (2010).
source.use: Product-form stationary law; complex balance is also checked from unit fluxes.

limits: The exact drift identity is analytical; the script checks n=1,...,30 and the fluxes as finite evidence. This only refutes the specified support-switch template under the given extension; it does not classify any stochastic behavior beyond the already identified product-form law.
